thread:
incident-bot: Pager — Unusual egress from prod-logdrain-1 to external endpoint (baton-analytics[.]com). 400+ POSTs in last 3m, ~120MB outbound. Possible misrouted log forwarder. @oliver oncall.

oliver (oncall): I'm awake, joining. Can someone confirm which cluster this is?

incident-bot: cluster: prod-us-west-2, node: ip-10-2-30-7, pod: logdrain-1 (namespace infra-logging). Sample http header shows `x-forwarded-host: baton-analytics.com` and API key header present.

maya (security): if there's an API key header that's bad. @luis can you check the pod mounts and service account tokens? Might be a broken helm values override from a customer env var.

luis (infra): Checking now. `kubectl -n infra-logging describe pod logdrain-1` shows a mounted secret `log-forwarder-creds`. Looks like a legacy `s3_write` key. I'm execing into the pod to validate outbound connections.

luis (infra): Exec output:
```
root@logdrain-1:/# netstat -tanp | grep ESTABLISHED | grep baton
tcp  0  0 10.2.30.7:45678 93.184.216.34:443 ESTABLISHED 1234/curl
```
So it's actively posting.

oliver (oncall): Step 1: isolate. luis, deny egress for this pod (NetworkPolicy + iptables) and scale down logdrain replicas to 0 for that daemonset.

luis (infra): Applied networkpolicy to block outbound HTTPS from infra-logging. Scaled logdrain DS to 0. `kubectl -n infra-logging scale ds/logdrain --replicas=0` ✅

maya (security): Good. Now we need to rotate any creds that were in that secret and treat them as potentially exfiltrated. @katy legal: does this meet threshold for customer notification? We saw only internal logs—no PII detected in quick grep, but need full search.

katy (legal): Put together scope: which tenants' logs routed through this drain? If only internal infra logs, we may not need full customer notif, but keep me in loop. Begin preserving artifacts and export chain-of-custody.

support-ops: We should prepare a notification template just in case — standby.

oliver (oncall): luis — rotate the `log-forwarder-creds` secret now, revoke the service principal access (IAM) tied to that secret, and rotate any AWS keys referenced.

luis (infra): Revoked IAM keys for svc-logdrain; created new secret and patched daemonset. Commands run:
```
aws iam update-access-key --access-key-id AKIA... --status Inactive
kubectl -n infra-logging patch secret log-forwarder-creds -p '{"data":{...}}'
```
New secret injected, but kept DS at 0 until we validate.

maya (security): Run quick grep for PII across last 24h logs in the index that was forwarded. I can query via internal ES cluster: `query: index:infra-logs source:logdrain* | grep -i 'ssn\\|email'` — preliminary results show no hits.

sre-bridge: Also check if KMS keys used to sign tokens were exposed. Where was the API key header issued from? It looked like a static header, probably long-lived.

luis (infra): The header came from the secret `log-forwarder-creds` — it contains a static API token for third-party ingestion. We'll rotate it and ask the vendor to invalidate any tokens on their side.

deploy-bot: Deploy succeeded: infra-logging secret rotated (deploy 8b9f). No pods restarted.

oliver (oncall): Next: full forensic dump from pod, preserved in secure bucket (compliant retention). @maya please run discovery on indexes to confirm no customer identifiers were included. @katy we'll prepare escalation notes.

maya (security): Forensics: pulled `/var/log/logdrain/*.log` and saved to s3://redwood-sec-incidents/5801234567/ — hashes computed and stored. Running a focused grep across the dump. ETA 30m.

support-ops: Prepped customer advisory draft (internal only). No outbound message until legal signs off.

oliver (oncall): Impact: we throttled/paused log drain for ~7m. No compute impact to inference runtime. Customers using external log forwarding may have a short window of missing logs but no model data accessed.

katy (legal): Based on current scope (internal logs only) and no PII hits, we do not require public notice. Hold decision until full grep completes. If any tenant data is found, escalate.

maya (security): Action items recorded:
- Isolate pod (done)
- Rotate secrets & revoke IAM (done)
- Forensic dump + grep (in progress)
- Vendor token invalidation request (outbound)
- Prepare customer/legal notes (pending)

oliver (oncall): I'll own the overnight watch. @luis take next 2 hours to finish vendor coordination. @maya keep me posted. If anything changes, please @oliver immediately.

incident-bot: Incident status -> Mitigated (containment) at 5801234600. Follow-up: postmortem + remediation ticket required.

oliver (oncall): Creating follow-up ticket and assigning to eng-infra + security for RCA and hardening (no static secrets in pod mounts, use short-lived tokens + IR policy). Handoff to morning oncall: @sre-bridge will pick up at 0800 PST.

sre-bridge: Acknowledged, will take lead at shift change. Thanks team :heart:
